home.title: KAPSULA — a cozy retro console emulator for Android
home.desc: PSP, PS1, Sega, NES and a dozen more consoles plus Java games — in one Android app. Free, no ads.
foot.legal: Emulation cores are open-source projects (PPSSPP, PCSX-ReARMed, Flycast and others) under GNU GPL; the full list and licenses are in the app: Settings → About. Console names belong to their owners and are used only to indicate compatibility.
home.lead: PSP, PS1, Sega, NES and a dozen more consoles — in one adorable app. Free and ad-free.
home.ios: KAPSULA lives only on Android — sadly, it won't run on iPhone.

get.sub: The download runs in your browser — you can close this window.
get.s1d: Tap “kapsula.apk” in your downloads or in the notification shade.
get.s2d: If your phone asks, allow installing from this browser. Just once.
get.s3d: Find KAPSULA on your home screen. I'm already waiting there.
con.lead: 16 consoles plus Java games. “Experimental” ones don't run on every phone or with every game.
con.own1: We don't distribute games or BIOS files and don't tell you where to get them. Dump your own disc or cartridge — and play. There are also free homebrew games that authors share online themselves.
con.own2: If a console needs a BIOS, KAPSULA will tell you which file and where to put it.

faq.lead: Don't be shy — here are the most common questions.
faq.q1: How do I install the APK?
faq.a1: Download the file and open it. If your phone asks about “unknown sources”, allow it for your browser. After that, KAPSULA will tell you when an update is out.
faq.q2: Will it run on my phone?
faq.a2: You need Android 8 or newer and a 64-bit processor — that's almost any phone from recent years. PS2 and Saturn need a more powerful phone. Check yours:
faq.q3: Why does it ask for access to all files?
faq.a3: So you can play straight from your folder without copying gigabytes. Don't want to? Don't grant it — you can add games by copying them.
faq.a4: Most often it's an archive (ZIP, 7Z, RAR) — unpack it first. Or a CUE file lost its BIN next to it. Check the file here:
faq.a5: Game saves fly to the cloud on their own. Install KAPSULA on a new phone, enter your player code — and continue right where you left off. You can turn it off in settings.
faq.q6: Can I play with a gamepad?
faq.a6: Yes. Connect it via Bluetooth or cable — KAPSULA picks it up and hides the on-screen buttons.
faq.a7: Profile, friends, tokens and saves — for the cloud. Statistics are anonymous and only with your consent. Details —
faq.a8: Yes. No ads, no purchases. Tokens are earned by playing.
faq.q9: Are there secrets on this site?
faq.a9: Maybe. Seivik loves being looked for… and not only him.

phone.h1: Will it run on my phone?
phone.lead: Pick your phone's processor — I'll tell you which consoles it can handle.
phone.where: The processor is listed in Settings → About phone (or “Specifications”).
phone.ph: For example: Snapdragon 778G, Helio G99, Dimensity 8100
phone.note: This is a rough estimate: a lot depends on the game, cooling and battery. Heavy PS2 and Saturn games don't run on every phone.

ck.bios.unkd: If it's PS1, it may not work: KAPSULA knows versions SCPH-1001, 5500, 5501, 5502, 7001, 101. If it's Saturn, it fits. MD5 fingerprint: {0}
ck.arcd: Unpack it first — inside you'll find the game image (ISO, CUE + BIN, CHD…). KAPSULA doesn't open archives.
ck.notgamed: A .{0} file is a description, picture or computer program.
ck.text: This is a text file, not a game
ck.textd: It contains text, while game images contain binary data.
ck.smalld: Only {0} — games aren't that tiny. Maybe the download didn't finish.
ck.bincue: If this is a disc image, a CUE file with the same name should sit next to it.
ck.pbp: PBP can also hold PS1 games — KAPSULA will tell them apart.
ck.chdd: Works for PS1, PS2, PSP, Dreamcast and Saturn. KAPSULA detects the console itself, and if it's wrong, you can change it on the game card.
ck.psxd: Most likely {0}. KAPSULA will detect it exactly from the disc.
ck.unkd: The .{0} extension shows no signs of a game. The file may be damaged, incomplete or renamed.

ck.cue0d: There are no FILE lines inside — the file is damaged.

priv.body:
Privacy

In short: KAPSULA doesn't collect your games, files or contacts. Only what's needed for your profile, friends and the cloud goes online — and you can turn it off. No ads, no trackers.

No sign-in, no registration

KAPSULA doesn't ask for your email, phone number or password. On first connection the app gets a random player code — that's how the server recognizes you. The code is stored on your phone; it can also restore your profile on a new phone. Don't show it to others.

What goes to the server and why

  • Profile — nickname, motto, chosen avatar, frame, banner and title, a showcase of favorite games (titles and consoles), badges. Visible to friends and to anyone who opens your profile by ID.
  • Progress — minutes played, number of saves and games, which consoles you play, daily streak, app version. Needed for levels, tokens, weekly challenges and anti-cheat.
  • Tokens and token purchases — balance and unlocked cosmetic items.
  • Friends — friends and requests, “cheering for you”, gifts to friends, “online” status.
  • Cloud saves — game save files (not the games and not save states), up to 2 MB per file. Turn off: Settings → Cloud saves.
  • “Invite to play” — an invitation with your phone's address in your home Wi-Fi network (so a friend can join the game over the network). Sent only to the friend you invited.
  • Anonymous statistics — only counters like “screen opened”, “game started on such-and-such console”, “there was a crash” — no game titles, no files and no player code; the server keeps daily totals. Only with your consent; turn off: Settings → Profile & cloud → Anonymous statistics.

What never leaves your phone

  • The games themselves, disc images, BIOS files, your files and photos.
  • Contacts, location, data from other apps.
  • Ads and trackers: KAPSULA has none.

Other sites the app contacts

  • Game covers — by title or disc code from the open libretro cover database (via GitHub). Turn off: Settings → Covers from the internet.
  • RetroAchievements — only if you sign in to RetroAchievements yourself: the app stores only the key they issue (not your password) and sends them achievement unlocks. Their rules are at retroachievements.org.
  • Updates — checking for a new version on the KAPSULA website, GitVerse and GitHub.

Where data is stored

The KAPSULA server runs on the Supabase cloud platform. Data is accessible only through server functions; the tables themselves are closed.

Deletion

Turn off the cloud and statistics in settings — no new data will be sent. You can delete your profile, cloud saves and progress from the server entirely in the app: Settings → Profile & cloud → “Delete profile”. If something goes wrong, contact us and include your player ID from the profile.

Changes

If KAPSULA starts sending anything new, we'll update this page and mention it in the version changelog.

Updated: November 26, 2026.
